title:
Possess Your
Possessions
paragraphs: Deliverance is God getting you out of Egypt. Holiness is God keeping you from going back. But possession is the part most believers never get to, because it requires something scarier than escaping or behaving — it requires you to walk onto the land and act like it's already yours. Obadiah doesn't end with Israel surviving Esau. He ends with the house of Jacob becoming fire and the house of Esau becoming stubble, because the same God who delivered you also armed you, and you've been sitting on the weapon.

Here's what nobody tells you about Esau's stubble: it doesn't fight back. Dry stalks don't negotiate with flame, they just burn, and that's exactly what your old defeat was always going to do the moment you stopped treating it like a threat and started treating it like kindling. You don't need a bigger miracle to possess what's yours. You need to stop standing at the property line holding the deed like a souvenir. Walk the land. The fire in you was never decorative — it was always meant to clear the field.
